title: The Dreaming Tent
text: A silk tent is pitched in the wilderness, empty and warm, smelling of home: bread, smoke, the soap your mother used. Nobody has pitched it. Anyone who sleeps in it, says the scrawl on the tent pole, dreams very clearly and does not always wake the same.

options.label: The most troubled lies down in the tent, longing for the peace it promises.

outcomes.text: The dream is gentle and long. They wake someone a little different, and lighter.
The dream is very clear. It returns every night after, and it is never gentle.

options.label: Take the silk. Whoever pitched it is not coming back for it.

outcomes.text: It is very good silk. It still smells of home.

options.label: Burn it before anyone gets ideas. Nothing that smells of home belongs out here.

outcomes.text: It burns with the smell of somebody's kitchen. From inside, a voice calls a name.
